statement: All four projects deploy to Azure; CI authenticates with GitHub OIDC federated credentials.
title: Target cloud is Azure for all four projects

rationale: Operator choice: zero infra, state travels with git, and the server can still enforce the guards a files-only approach cannot.
statement: tools/stf-mcp: in-memory SQLite rebuilt from .stf/export/*.json (byte-stable, committed); no server infra.
title: Control plane is a local stdio MCP server over SQLite with a committed JSON export

rationale: Operator choice at bootstrap; spec 001 Q-003 revisits publishing individual projects publicly.
statement: github.com/cjsy2001/secops-task-factory is private; project code lives under projects/<name>/.
title: One private monorepo: factory + the four projects as specs

consequences: Next steps: (2) package the factory as a plugin; (3) add an optional explicit seq to stf_charter_spec so specs keep 001-004; (4) re-charter each spec in its new repo and re-capture its questions and decisions (their IDs will be reissued). D-001 (Azure) and D-002 (plane design) stay factory-wide. Until the move, CLAUDE.md, README, .claude/rules path globs (projects/**) and spec Assumptions that name secops-task-factory or projects/<name> are stale, and must be updated when each spec moves. Recall and memory are no longer shared across projects. Every public repo needs gitleaks (pre-commit hook and CI) active from its first commit.
rationale: stf's evidence checks only work inside a single git root: repoRelative refuses paths outside the root, and commitExists/inGitHistory run git in the plane's own repo. The plane therefore has to live with the code it verifies. Public project repos give recruiters visible history, and GitHub code scanning is free for public repos (spec 001 Assumptions). This is the cheapest moment to move: every spec is at clarify, with 0 tasks, 0 artefact hashes and no projects/ folder. After implementation starts, extraction would rewrite recorded commit shas and move artefact paths.
statement: Each project (devsecops-pipeline, hardened-iac, malware-sandbox, zero-trust-audit) moves to its own GitHub repo, public from the first commit. Each repo holds its code at the root, its specs/, its own .stf/export/ plane and its project rules. github.com/cjsy2001/secops-task-factory stays private and holds the stf MCP server, skills, hooks and rule templates, packaged as a Claude Code plugin, plus a plane for factory-level work.
title: One public repo per project; the factory stays private as a plugin

consequences: Don't propose embeddings for recall or search. If retrieval quality becomes a problem, improve tags, titles and FTS queries first.
rationale: Operator scope call (2026-09-25): honest, local, simple tooling over AI-factory features. Full-text memory is enough as long as it works across sessions, and its results are reproducible from the committed export.
statement: stf memory and recall stay local and deterministic: SQLite FTS5 memories, /stf:memory, /stf:handoff and the SessionStart recall block. No embedding model, no vector index.
title: No AI embeddings or vector search in stf

consequences: Cross-repo views (e.g. a portfolio hub) are built from each repo's committed export or its published pages, never from a shared live service.
rationale: Operator scope call (2026-09-25). Keeps D-002's properties: zero infrastructure, state travels with git, and every evidence claim can be re-checked from a checkout.
statement: Each repo's plane is in-memory SQLite rebuilt from its committed .stf/export/. There is no Azure-hosted plane and no authentication layer.
title: The plane stays local: no hosted plane, no auth

rationale: Operator scope call (2026-09-25). A server that rewrites unreviewed content would undermine the refusals and hashed evidence the factory exists for.
statement: stf finds problems through stf_verify, the analyze gate and write refusals, and reports them. The server never repairs content on its own; fixes go through the owning skill. Any automation runs through Claude Code /loop or scheduled agents, and tracked changes through change requests (Roadmap P1-2).
title: Detection without server-side auto-fix

rationale: Operator (2026-09-25) wanted a simple view instead of reading JSON (Roadmap P1-7). It reads through the store's pure render, so it can't change the plane.
statement: stf dashboard (make dashboard) renders the plane as one self-contained, read-only HTML page at .stf/dashboard.html (gitignored), titled per repo.
title: A read-only HTML dashboard of the plane

consequences: A repo turns status pages on by creating .stf/pages.json and off by deleting it. devsecops-pipeline dropped scripts/status-pages and its project hook (devsecops-pipeline#2).
rationale: One implementation for every project repo instead of drifting copies; TypeScript with marked removes the Python/uv dependency. On devsecops-pipeline spec 001 the port reproduced the Python output's ids and in-page links exactly.
statement: The plugin provides stf spec-page, stf hub and stf pages, the skill stf:pages, and a PostToolUse hook that rebuilds the pages after stf plane writes. The hook is a silent no-op unless the repo has both .stf/export/ and .stf/pages.json. Each repo commits only .stf/pages.json (artifact URLs without share keys). Publishing stays with Claude.
title: Status pages ship in the plugin; each repo keeps only .stf/pages.json

consequences: A plugin older than the moved column can't load a plane that has it, so every repo using stf needs the update. Spec 001 is marked moved to cjsy2001/devsecops-pipeline#1.
rationale: Operator (2026-09-25): a real moved state, linked to D-004, with history intact. Without it the old rows read as live work at clarify and could still be written to.
statement: stf_move_spec records {repo, seq, decision, reason} on a spec that now lives in another repo's plane. Its questions, decisions, alternatives, evidence and events stay readable here; every new lifecycle, task, run, capture, event and handoff write on it is refused with spec_moved. Status, recall and the pages show "moved → repo#seq"; verify skips it. Specs 002–004 are marked when their repos exist.
title: Moved specs keep their history and refuse new writes

consequences: Changes to the standard project setup are made once, in tools/stf-mcp/src/templates/project, and reach every later project.
rationale: Operator (2026-09-25). The scaffold is devsecops-pipeline's first commit made generic; rendered for devsecops-pipeline it matches a8ece62 except for the project text, one generic security bullet and the status-page .gitignore lines.
statement: stf new-project (and the skill stf:new-project) scaffolds a project repo: git on main with the gitleaks pre-commit hook and secrets CI job, stf plugin config, security/azure/factory rules, CLAUDE.md, README, Makefile and MIT license, an empty plane and spec 001 chartered at setup. Defaults: public, Azure rules, MIT. The skill makes the first commit through the hook and asks before each GitHub step (create and push, check the secrets run, protect main).
title: New projects come from stf new-project

consequences: Recording a factory-wide decision includes updating the templates or rules that carry it to projects.
rationale: Operator (2026-09-25). This is the only place factory-wide decisions are recorded, factory sessions keep recall, and CI's round-trip and verify checks run against a real plane.
statement: secops-task-factory keeps .stf/export/ for factory-wide decisions, work on the plugin itself, and the history of moved specs. A moved spec's folder under specs/ may be deleted here (verify skips it, git keeps the file). Constraints that every project must follow reach the projects through the scaffold templates and .claude/rules, because project planes can't read this one.
title: The factory repo keeps its own plane for factory-level work

consequences: Read a8ece62 in D-011 and ALT-021 as 05dc3cd. The plane recorded no commit SHAs in checkpoints or evidence, so stf_verify is unaffected. GitHub's PR refs (9 in secops-task-factory, 2 in devsecops-pipeline) still point at the pre-rewrite commits. That was accepted rather than asking GitHub Support to purge them.
rationale: Operator (2026-10-27): the repos are a public personal portfolio, and the employer email shouldn't be in their history. Plane records are append-only, so the old SHA is noted here instead of editing D-011. a8ece62 now resolves only through devsecops-pipeline's PR refs and the local pre-rewrite backup.
statement: On 2026-10-27 the commit authors in secops-task-factory, devsecops-pipeline and ctf-writeups were rewritten to the operator's personal email with git filter-repo, and the result was force-pushed to main. The file trees are unchanged, but every commit SHA changed. devsecops-pipeline's scaffold commit, which D-011 and ALT-021 cite as a8ece62, is now 05dc3cd. D-011 itself still stands.
title: Commit authors rewritten to the personal email; D-011 and ALT-021 cite a pre-rewrite SHA

consequences: Supersedes D-004, whose project rule this restates; only the factory's visibility changes. Install docs drop the "private repo, gh auth first" notes, and the project scaffold template no longer calls the factory private. The live viewer and docs/using-stf.md are served from this repo by GitHub Pages. GitHub's old PR refs keep the pre-rewrite author email, as accepted in D-013.
rationale: Operator (2026-10-27) asked for the factory to be usable in other people's repos. Claude Code installs a plugin by cloning its marketplace repo, so a private factory can't be installed by anyone outside it. D-004's per-project reasoning still holds and is carried over unchanged: stf's evidence checks only work inside one git root, so each plane lives with the code it verifies. Before the switch, the full history was scanned with gitleaks (no leaks) and commit authors were rewritten to the personal email (D-013).
statement: Each project moves to its own GitHub repo, public from the first commit, holding its code at the root, its specs/, its own .stf/export/ plane and its project rules. github.com/cjsy2001/secops-task-factory is public as well, MIT-licensed (made public 2026-10-27). It holds the stf MCP server, skills, hooks and rule templates, packaged as a Claude Code plugin that anyone can install from its marketplace, plus a plane for factory-level work. Its main branch is protected (secrets and plane checks required, PRs only, no force pushes).
title: One public repo per project; the factory repo is public too, as an installable plugin
